q-fbc2e014d03f: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little about yourself.
a-0d268618a916: Hi, my name is Dory Han. I live alone in a small apartment in Mapo, Seoul, and I've been living there for about three years now. My weekdays are pretty busy, but I try to keep some time for myself in the evenings and on weekends. There's a park along the Han River near my place, so I often go there for a walk or a light jog. I'm happy to tell you more about myself today.
q-5fa6b79b05fb: I'd like to know about where you live. Describe your home. What does it look like?
a-f023f015eeaf: I live alone in a small apartment in Mapo, Seoul. It's on the seventh floor of a twelve-story building, and it has one bedroom and a living room with an open kitchen. When you walk in, you see the living room right away. There's a gray sofa, a small TV, and a bookshelf against the wall. The window is quite big, so I get a lot of sunlight during the day, and I can even see a bit of the Han River from there. In the bedroom, I have a bed and a desk, and on the desk I keep my laptop and a small speaker for music. It's not big, but it's just the right size for one person. My favorite spot is by the living room window. In the evening, I sit there and listen to music, and it really helps me unwind after a long day.
q-495180f57cf2: What do you usually do at home? Tell me about a typical day at home, including any chores you do.
a-db90f647f8ab: Since I live alone, all the housework is on me. On weekdays, I get up, make my bed, and have a quick breakfast, usually coffee and toast, before I leave. When I get home in the evening, I change my clothes first and then cook dinner. I'm not a great cook, so I usually make something simple like fried rice or pasta. After eating, I do the dishes right away, because if I put it off, I really don't want to do it the next day. Then I sit on the sofa and relax, watching Netflix or listening to music. On weekends, I do the bigger chores. On Saturday morning, I vacuum, mop the floor, and do a week's worth of laundry. Once the laundry is hanging up to dry, the place feels organized, and that makes me feel good. After that, I take it easy for the rest of the weekend.
q-46b1e3c0109d: Tell me about a problem you had at home. What happened, and how did you solve it?
a-3e6b16129e02: I remember something that happened last winter. One evening I came home, and the apartment was freezing. I turned on the boiler, but nothing happened. There was just an error code on the screen. At first I thought I had pressed something wrong, so I looked through the manual, but that didn't help. So I called the building management office, and they said they would send a repairman the next morning. That night I slept under two thick blankets, and it was still really cold. The next day, the repairman came and found that one part had broken, and he replaced it in about thirty minutes. Since then, I always turn on the boiler once before winter starts, just to check it. Living alone, I learned that in the end, I have to handle these things myself.
q-602a7fd72c06: Tell me about the home you lived in when you were a child. How was that home different from the home you live in now? Please describe the differences in as much detail as possible.
a-9ec1ee81d5b4: When I was a child, I lived with my parents and my younger brother in an old two-story house just outside Seoul. It was very different from where I live now. First of all, it was much bigger. It had three bedrooms, a living room, and even a small yard where my mom grew lettuce and peppers. But I had to share a room with my brother, so I never really had my own space. The house was also pretty old, so it was cold in winter, and we used to wear thick socks and sweaters inside. My apartment now is the opposite. It's small, but it's modern and warm, and every corner of it is mine. The biggest difference, though, is the sound. Back then, the house was always noisy with my family talking, cooking, and watching TV. Now it's really quiet when I get home. I love the freedom, but honestly, sometimes I miss that noise.
q-5af6b26e440b: Tell me about your favorite room in your home. What does it look like, and why do you like it?
a-3e715bb29bd0: My favorite room is the living room, especially the spot by the window. My apartment is small, so the living room is also my dining room and my home theater. There's a gray sofa, a small TV, and a bookshelf against the wall. The window is quite big, so the room gets a lot of sunlight during the day, and I can even see a bit of the Han River from there. Last summer, I moved the sofa right next to the window, and since then it has been the best seat in the house. In the evening, I sit there with a cup of tea, put on some quiet music on my Bluetooth speaker, and watch the lights come on across the river. On weekends, I sometimes spend the whole afternoon there, reading or watching a movie. It's not fancy, but it's the place where I can finally relax after a long day. That's why I like it the most.
q-3619d27f3c9d: Tell me about a change you made to your home recently. What did you change, why did you change it, and how do you feel about it now?
a-9bfe518dc750: The biggest change I made recently was rearranging my living room. It happened last summer. I was supposed to go on a trip to Busan, but it got canceled, so I suddenly had a free week at home. I had been wanting to organize my apartment for a long time, so I started with the closet and threw away a lot of old clothes. Then I looked at the living room and realized the sofa was in the wrong place. It was against the wall, facing away from the window. So I pushed it next to the window, moved the bookshelf to the other side, and bought a small floor lamp online. It took a whole afternoon, and I was sweating a lot, because I did everything by myself. But when I finished, the room felt like a completely different space. It looks bigger and brighter now. These days, I spend most of my evenings on that sofa, so I'm really glad I made the change.
q-e92eb1ceb3d3: You indicated that you like to watch movies. What kind of movies do you like, and why?
a-806e23ef517c: My favorite kinds of movies are science fiction and action. I like sci-fi movies because they show me worlds I could never see in real life. When I watch something about space, the future, or time travel, I feel like I've been somewhere completely different for two hours. I especially like Christopher Nolan's movies, because the stories are complicated and they keep me thinking long after the movie ends. Action movies are a different story. After a long, tiring week, I just want to clear my head, and action movies are fun to watch without thinking too hard. On the other hand, I'm not good with horror movies. When I see a scary scene, it stays in my head for days and I can't sleep well. So when my friends suggest a horror movie, I usually suggest something else.
q-ace7541367cd: Tell me about the movie theater you usually go to. What do you typically do before and after watching a movie?
a-c68fc57eb096: I usually go to a multiplex theater that's two subway stops from my apartment. It's on the top floor of a shopping mall, so there's a lot to do before and after the movie. I usually go on Saturday evenings, and I book my ticket in advance on my phone. I always pick a seat a little behind the middle, because I can see the whole screen comfortably from there. I arrive about thirty minutes early and buy popcorn and a coke. I only eat caramel popcorn. Without it, something feels missing. After the movie, I don't go straight home. I go to a cafe in the same building. If I go with a friend, we talk about the movie we just saw, and if I go alone, I read other people's reviews on my phone. Honestly, talking about the movie afterward is almost as fun as the movie itself.
q-03ded0dbdc31: Tell me about the most memorable movie you have ever seen. What was it about, and why was it so memorable?
a-b9583c5fd721: The most memorable movie I've ever seen is Interstellar. I first saw it when I was in college, with a friend, at an IMAX theater. It's about a future where the Earth is slowly becoming impossible to live on, and the main character goes into space to find a new planet for humanity. But time passes differently in space, so when he comes back, his little daughter has already become older than he is. That scene hit me really hard, and I couldn't take my eyes off the screen. I remember that after the movie, my friend and I talked for two hours about time and family. Since then, I've watched it at least five more times, and every time I notice something new. To me, it's not just a science fiction movie. It's really a story about family.
q-f19bff4711ea: Tell me about the last time you went to see a movie. What did you do before, during, and after the movie? Describe that day from beginning to end.
a-e4e491c40e7e: The last time I went to the movies was two weekends ago. I went with a close friend to see a new sci-fi movie that everyone was talking about. We met at the mall around five, and since we had already booked the tickets on the app, we had plenty of time. First, we had a quick dinner at a noodle place on the same floor. Then we bought caramel popcorn and cokes and went in about ten minutes early. The movie was almost three hours long, but it didn't feel long at all. The visuals were amazing, and during the last scene the theater was so quiet that I could hear people holding their breath. When it ended, some people even clapped. After that, we went to a cafe downstairs and talked about the ending for over an hour, because we had understood it differently. I got home around eleven, and I looked up other people's interpretations online before I went to bed. It was a simple day, but a really satisfying one.
q-22eb8022f03d: Who is your favorite actor or actress? Tell me about a news story you heard about that person. What was it about, and why was it interesting to you?
a-bfa8fe7e404c: My favorite actor is Cillian Murphy. He's an Irish actor, and I first noticed him in Christopher Nolan's movies. He appears in many of Nolan's films, like Inception and Dunkirk, but usually in small roles. What I like about him is his eyes. He doesn't say much, but you can read everything on his face. The news I remember best about him is that he won the Academy Award for Best Actor for Oppenheimer. It was his first leading role in a Nolan movie after almost twenty years of supporting roles, so when I heard the news, I was really happy for him. I watched his acceptance speech online, and he seemed so humble and a little shy. I also read that he stays away from social media and lives a quiet life with his family. I think that's why I trust him as an actor. He's famous for his work, not for his private life.
q-2a20575eeab2: You said you like going to parks. Describe a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
a-83f8b573693a: The park I go to most often is Hangang Park, which is about a ten-minute walk from my place. As the name says, it's a long park that runs along the Han River. There's a bike path and a walking path side by side along the water, and next to them there's a wide grassy area. In spring and fall, people spread out mats on the grass, eat fried chicken, or just lie down and relax. There's a convenience store too, so you can buy some noodles or a drink and eat while looking at the river. Around the middle of the park, there's a small stage where people sometimes do street performances on weekends. My favorite time is around sunset. The river turns orange, and the lights in the buildings across the water come on one by one. It's really beautiful. Even though it's in the middle of the city, I feel calm whenever I'm there.
q-87949a7524d2: What do you usually do when you go to the park? Who do you go with, and how often do you go?
a-d84ac8648c04: I go there two or three times a week. On weekdays, I usually go alone. After dinner, I walk or jog lightly for about thirty minutes. Walking along the river with music in my earphones really melts away the stress of the day. On weekends, I often go with friends. We meet in the afternoon, spread out a mat, and order fried chicken and beer through a delivery app. Then we just talk for hours. That's a really common weekend scene in Seoul. When the weather is nice, we sometimes rent bikes and ride along the river to the next park and back. And sometimes I just sit on a bench and do nothing but look at the river. For me, the park is a place to exercise, a place to meet friends, and a place to be alone, all at the same time.
q-23654fe2c3d7: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, and what happened?
a-a682adb7185e: The most memorable one was the fireworks festival at Hangang Park two years ago in the fall. I went with three friends, and we got there at three in the afternoon to grab a spot. The fireworks didn't start until seven, so we waited for four hours. And the crowd was unbelievable. There was barely any room to stand on the grass, and the line for the restroom was thirty minutes long. To be honest, while we were waiting, I wondered why we had even come. But once the fireworks started, that feeling disappeared completely. The fireworks exploded over the river and reflected on the water. It was absolutely spectacular. Everyone around us was cheering at the same time, and even though they were strangers, it felt like we were all one big group. It took an hour to get to the subway station afterward, but nobody complained. It was a tiring day, but it was worth every minute.
q-b995807fd5c0: You said you enjoy listening to music. What kind of music do you like, and who is your favorite singer?
a-bf49f7729626: I mostly listen to ballads and pop music. I especially like songs with good lyrics. The melody matters, of course, but when the lyrics really touch me, I end up listening to that song on repeat for months. My favorite singer is IU. She has a clear, warm voice, and she writes a lot of her own songs, so each one has her own story in it. She has sad songs and bright songs, so I can pick one depending on my mood that day. I usually listen to pop music when I'm working out or cleaning. When I put on something with a fast beat, my body just starts moving on its own. On the other hand, I don't really listen to loud rock or heavy metal. For me, music is more about calming me down than getting me excited.
q-d66fd08dc278: When and where do you usually listen to music? What do you use to listen to it?
a-b9b6e5f79092: I listen to music pretty much all day. My day starts with music on the subway, through my wireless earphones. I need something upbeat in the morning to wake up. When I get home, I play music on a small Bluetooth speaker in the living room. Cooking dinner or doing the dishes is a lot less boring with music on. Before bed, I lie down and listen to quiet ballads at a low volume. I use a streaming app, and I've made a few playlists, one for mornings, one for working out, and one for nighttime, and I switch between them depending on the situation. I also like that the app recommends new songs based on my taste. One of my current favorite songs is one I found that way. Honestly, I can't imagine a day without music.
q-2d87a8250749: How did you first become interested in music? Has your taste in music changed over the years?
a-6bb41ed2b7a5: I got into music when I was in middle school. I got my first MP3 player as a gift, and I filled it with the idol songs my friends were listening to and played them all day. Back then, I only liked fast, exciting songs. In high school, I had to listen while studying, so I started listening to piano pieces without lyrics and quiet pop. But the biggest change came in my mid-twenties. I was going through a hard time, and I happened to hear a ballad by IU. The lyrics felt like they were about my own life, and I played it over and over that night. Since then, I've had the habit of really paying attention to lyrics. These days, I listen to songs that comfort me much more than songs that get me excited. Looking back, I think my taste in music has always reflected where I was in my life at the time.
q-e570d4a59d5e: Tell me about a memorable time when you heard live music. When and where was it, who were you with, and what made it so special?
a-22e64de5fc19: The most memorable time I heard live music was at IU's concert at Olympic Park about three years ago. I went with a friend from college who likes her as much as I do. It was the first concert I had ever managed to get tickets for, so it was special just for that. But the truly unforgettable moment came in the middle of the show. IU suddenly started singing without any music, and tens of thousands of people all held their breath and listened. I couldn't believe such a huge venue could become that quiet. I had listened to that song hundreds of times through my earphones, but live, it felt like a completely different song. During the last song, the whole audience waved their light sticks and sang along, and I got goosebumps all over. When we walked out afterward, my friend and I couldn't say a word for a while. Since that day, every time I hear that song, that moment comes right back to me.
q-b91ac9781f65: You indicated that you jog. Where do you usually go jogging? Describe the place.
a-0f3b2d70847f: I jog on the riverside path at Hangang Park near my apartment. The path is flat and runs for several kilometers along the river, so it's perfect for running. There are no traffic lights, so I never have to stop, and the path is wide enough that I don't have to worry about bumping into bikes. There are streetlights all along the path, so it's bright even at night, and there are always other runners around, so it feels safe. I also like that there are distance markers every five hundred meters, so I can see right away how far I've run. On one side there's the river, and on the other side there's grass and trees, so the view never gets boring. Under the bridge where I turn around, there's a water fountain and a restroom. There are lots of good places to run in Seoul, but for me, this one is the best.
q-49f2a65896bc: Tell me about your jogging routine. How often do you jog, and what do you do before and after?
a-94eb76bbedca: I jog three times a week, usually on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. On weekdays, I go out around eight after a light dinner, and on Saturdays I go in the morning when the park is less crowded. Before I go, I change into my workout clothes, turn on a running app on my phone, and put on some fast music through my earphones. When I get to the park, I stretch for about five minutes and walk slowly before I start running. I usually run about five kilometers in a little over thirty minutes. I'm not fast, but my goal is to be consistent, so I don't worry about speed. When I finish, I walk for another five minutes to catch my breath and stretch my legs. After I get home, take a shower, and drink lots of water, I feel completely refreshed. And on the days I run, I sleep much better.
q-3260b4a4bd6c: How did you start jogging? Tell me about a memorable experience you had while jogging.
a-2ab63962e486: I started jogging two years ago after I got the results of my health checkup. The doctor told me I needed to exercise more, but a gym costs money and I wasn't confident I would keep going. So I chose running, because it's free. In the beginning, I couldn't even run one kilometer without walking. The day I remember most is the first time I ran five kilometers without stopping. It was about two months after I started. That day my legs felt light for some reason, so I just kept going. When the app announced five kilometers, I shouted without thinking, and a man running next to me laughed and gave me a thumbs-up. It might sound like a small thing, but for me it was a huge achievement. Since that day, I've believed that if I keep at something, I can do anything.
q-c513d2f11461: Have you ever been injured while jogging? Tell me what happened. What do you do to avoid getting hurt, and what advice would you give to someone who wants to start jogging?
a-7c4c913e47b9: Yes, I got hurt once, about a year ago. It was a cold evening, and I was in a hurry, so I skipped my stretching and started running right away. After about two kilometers, I stepped on the edge of the path and twisted my ankle. It hurt so much that I had to walk home very slowly. The next day, my ankle was swollen, so I went to see a doctor. Luckily, it wasn't serious, but he told me to rest for two weeks. It was frustrating, because I had just built up a good routine. Since then, I never skip my warm-up. I stretch for at least five minutes and walk for a while before I start running. I also bought proper running shoes, because my old sneakers were worn out. So my advice for beginners is simple. Always warm up, start slowly, and don't push yourself too hard in the first month. Being consistent is much more important than being fast.
q-b5ce927a37ef: You indicated that you like to walk. Where and when do you usually walk, who do you walk with, and why do you enjoy it?
a-99efbb852a3b: I walk almost every day, usually along the river at Hangang Park near my apartment. On the days I don't jog, I go out after dinner and walk for about forty minutes. I usually walk alone, because it's my time to clear my head. I put in my earphones and listen to music or a podcast, and I don't look at my phone at all. The path is flat and well lit, so it's safe even at night, and there are always other people walking their dogs or exercising. On weekends, I sometimes walk with a friend instead of going to a cafe. We buy a coffee, walk along the river for an hour, and talk about everything. What I like about walking is that it's easy. I don't need special clothes or equipment, and it never feels like too much. After a walk, I feel refreshed, and I sleep better. For me, it's the simplest way to stay healthy.
q-3621858ff192: You said you like to travel domestically. Where do you like to go in your country, and what is it like?
a-d9db75f05918: My favorite place to travel in Korea is Gangneung, on the east coast. It's only two hours from Seoul by high-speed train, so it's perfect for a weekend trip. Gangneung is famous for the East Sea, and the water is really clear and blue. There are cafes lined up along the beach, and my favorite thing to do there is to sit with a coffee and look at the ocean. Actually, Gangneung is known as a coffee city because it has so many famous cafes. The food is great too. You can eat fresh raw fish right in front of the sea, and dishes made with local potatoes and corn are delicious. It gets crowded in summer, but the winter beach is quiet and has a nice atmosphere. To be honest, I like Gangneung in winter even more. Walking on an empty beach and then stepping into a warm cafe is all I need to feel rested.
q-1c42e79587c3: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip? Tell me about the things you do before you leave.
a-87970256f539: I like to prepare for trips well in advance. Once I decide on the dates, the first thing I do is book my train or plane tickets, because the earlier you buy, the cheaper they are. Then I look for a place to stay. I read the reviews carefully on an app and choose one with a good location. I prefer places with a nice view, so if a room looks out on the ocean or the mountains, I don't mind paying a little more. After that, I search social media and blogs for good restaurants and cafes and save them in my map app. I don't plan too tightly. I just pick two or three must-visit places for each day. I pack the night before I leave, and I always use a checklist. I once left my charger at home, and I've used a checklist ever since. Finally, before I walk out the door, I check the gas and the windows and water my plants.
q-06db42bf922c: Tell me about a memorable trip you took in your country. Where did you go, who did you go with, and what made it special?
a-18f5f9983cc3: The trip I remember most is the one I took to Jeju Island last spring with two friends from college. It was the first time the three of us had traveled together since graduation. We rented a car and drove around the island for four days. On the first day, we drove along the east coast and saw fields of yellow canola flowers with the blue sea behind them. It looked just like a painting. On the second day, we challenged ourselves to climb Hallasan, the highest mountain in Korea. It took nine hours to go up and come back down, and it was exhausting. But when we saw the crater lake at the top, we forgot all about the pain. The grilled black pork we had that evening was the best dinner of my life. On our last night, we sat in the yard of our guesthouse drinking beer and talking about old times until dawn. The scenery was beautiful, but the best part of the trip was getting close to my old friends again.
q-bae06e0ea2ac: Tell me about a trip you took when you were young. Where did you go, who did you go with, and what did you see or do there?
a-4d375011ee39: When I was about ten, my family went to Gyeongju for summer vacation. Gyeongju is an old capital city in the southeast of Korea, and it's full of historic sites. We drove there in my dad's car, and it took almost five hours. My brother and I fought in the back seat the whole way. I remember we visited a famous temple called Bulguksa and saw huge ancient tombs that looked like green hills. To be honest, I was too young to appreciate the history. What I really loved was the hotel swimming pool and the ice cream my dad bought us every afternoon. One night, we rode bikes around a pond with beautiful lights, and that scene still stays in my mind. Looking back, it was one of the few trips where my whole family was together for several days. These days we're all busy, so that memory feels more precious as I get older.
q-22976e5fbda6: You mentioned that you like traveling abroad. Which countries have you been to, and which one did you like the most?
a-fdf138d14554: I've been to Japan, Thailand, and a few countries in Europe. The place I've visited most often is Japan. It's only a two-hour flight from Seoul, the food suits my taste, and the streets are clean, so I always feel comfortable there. I especially like Osaka. The city is lively and the people are friendly. Just walking down Dotonbori street eating takoyaki and okonomiyaki makes me feel like I'm really on vacation. Thailand is cheap and warm, so it's a good place to rest in winter. Europe has beautiful buildings and history, but the flight takes over twelve hours, so it's hard to go often. Next time, I'd like to visit somewhere close with great food, like Taiwan or Vietnam. For me, the best part of traveling abroad is eating the local food right where it comes from.
q-016e7d51c1b0: What do you do to get ready for an overseas trip? What do you usually take with you?
a-84a3a7448b9d: Getting ready for an overseas trip is similar to a domestic one, but there are a few extra things. First, I check my passport's expiration date, because many countries require at least six months left on it. I usually book flights two or three months ahead, and I choose a hotel near the airport or close to a subway station. About a week before I leave, I exchange money at the bank, and these days I also bring a card that works overseas. I also sign up for a local SIM card or roaming in advance, because if my map app doesn't work, I'm in real trouble. I pack as light as I can. I bring clothes for just a few days, but I never forget my charger, a travel adapter, and some basic medicine, since going to a hospital abroad is difficult. Finally, I take photos of my passport and tickets and save them on my phone, just in case I lose them.
q-6b166d3d2e69: Tell me about the most memorable trip abroad you have taken. What happened during the trip?
a-3acd9a2f41a9: The most memorable one was a solo trip to Osaka last November. It was my first time traveling abroad alone, so I was a little nervous before I left. But on the second evening, something unforgettable happened. I walked into a tiny ramen shop, and the whole menu was in Japanese, so I just stood there not knowing what to order. Then an elderly Japanese man sitting next to me spoke to me in English. His English wasn't perfect, but he explained each item on the menu with gestures and a translation app on his phone. In the end, I ordered the tonkotsu ramen he recommended, and it was amazing. After the meal, he even told me about a small shrine nearby that most tourists don't know about. I went there the next day, and it was so quiet and beautiful. Since that trip, I'm not afraid of traveling alone anymore. It's funny, but a stranger's kindness is what I remember most about that trip, even more than the food.
q-826c16945004: Where do people in your country like to go when they travel abroad? Why do they like those places?
a-0030fb326b71: These days, Koreans travel abroad a lot, and the most popular destination is definitely Japan. It's only about two hours away by plane, the food is great, and it's relatively affordable. So many people visit cities like Osaka, Fukuoka, or Tokyo just for a long weekend. Southeast Asia is also very popular, especially Vietnam and Thailand. People go to places like Da Nang or Bangkok because prices are low and the weather is warm, so they're perfect for relaxing at a resort. Families with kids often choose Guam for similar reasons. For longer holidays, some people go to Europe or the United States, but those trips are expensive and the flights are long, so they're more of a once-in-a-while thing. In general, I think Koreans prefer places that are close, safe, and known for good food, because most people can only take short vacations.
q-4e69cf663ebb: Tell me about your first trip abroad, or the first time you traveled abroad by yourself. Where did you go, and what do you remember most about it?
a-8df7ba967541: My first trip abroad on my own was to Osaka last November. Before that, I had always traveled with my family or friends, so I was pretty nervous before I left. I worried about getting lost and about eating alone. But on the second evening, something unforgettable happened. I walked into a tiny ramen shop, and the whole menu was in Japanese, so I just stood there not knowing what to order. Then an elderly Japanese man sitting next to me spoke to me in English. His English wasn't perfect, but he explained each item on the menu with gestures and a translation app on his phone. In the end, I ordered the tonkotsu ramen he recommended, and it was amazing. After the meal, he even told me about a small shrine nearby that most tourists don't know about. I went there the next day, and it was so quiet and beautiful. Since that trip, I'm not afraid of traveling alone anymore. Actually, I think you meet more people like him when you travel by yourself.
q-a519c021a268: You said you sometimes spend your vacation at home. What do you usually do during a vacation at home?
a-9fb3fc50e23d: I also enjoy staying home during my vacation instead of going somewhere. q-55b9edd725fc: Pick two different kinds of music or two musicians you like. Compare them and explain their similarities and differences in as much detail as possible.

Dance pop, on the other hand, is all about energy. The beat is fast, the melody is catchy, and the lyrics are usually simple and repetitive. q-17d329ef73f5: Tell me about some new electronic gadgets or equipment that people who like music are interested in these days. What are they, and why are people excited about them?
a-b112e4486e66: These days, I think the gadget music lovers talk about most is wireless earphones with noise canceling. A few years ago, most people used the wired earphones that came free with their phones. But now, almost everyone on the subway wears wireless ones. People are excited about noise canceling because it blocks out the noise of the subway or the street, so you can enjoy music at a low volume, which is also better for your ears. I bought a pair last year, and it completely changed my subway rides. Another thing people are interested in is smart speakers. You just say the name of a song, and it plays right away, which is really handy when you're cooking. And of course, streaming apps keep getting smarter. They use AI to recommend songs based on what you've listened to. I think in the future, we probably won't need separate devices at all. Everything will be connected, and music will just follow us from room to room.
q-13dc58236989: Compare the movies made today to the movies you watched when you were young. How have movies changed over the years? Give me specific examples.
a-966d3541432f: Movies have changed a lot since I was young. When I was a kid, special effects were quite simple, so you could easily tell that the monsters or spaceships were fake. The stories were usually simple, too. There was a good hero and a bad villain, and the ending was happy. And to watch a movie, we had to go to a theater or rent a video or a DVD from a shop. These days, the computer graphics are so realistic that you can't tell what's real. The stories have become more complicated as well. For example, it's hard to fully understand a Christopher Nolan movie after watching it just once. The way we watch has changed, too. Now people watch movies at home anytime on streaming services like Netflix. Another big change is Korean cinema. For example, Parasite won Best Picture at the Academy Awards, and now people all over the world watch Korean movies. Personally, I love the new technology, but sometimes I miss the simple fun of old movies.
q-8b392334e37f: What issues about movies do people talk about these days? Tell me about a recent trend or concern in the movie industry and what people think about it.
a-3d09f5bf9789: The issue my friends and I talk about most these days is that fewer people are going to movie theaters. The biggest reason is the price. Ticket prices have gone up a lot in the last few years, so for two people with popcorn, it gets pretty expensive. On the other hand, a streaming service costs about the same as one movie ticket for a whole month. So a lot of people say, "Why go to the theater? It'll be on Netflix soon." Some people worry that small theaters will close down if this continues. Others are happy, because they can watch more movies comfortably at home. In my opinion, we need both. Dramas and comedies are fine at home, but sci-fi and action movies should be seen on a big screen with great sound. I think theaters will survive in the future by offering experiences you can't get at home, like IMAX.
q-8c11bea559a1: Tell me how homes in your country have changed over the past five or ten years. What were homes like before, and what are they like now?
a-8f41f70dd001: Homes in Korea have changed a lot over the past ten or twenty years. In the past, many families lived in low houses with a small yard, like the one I grew up in. They were spacious, but they were old, cold in winter, and hard to take care of. These days, most people live in high-rise apartments. In any city, you can see apartment complexes that look exactly the same. One of the biggest changes is the size. More and more people live alone, like me, so there are a lot more studios and small apartments now. The technology is different, too. Now we open the door with a password or a fingerprint instead of a key, and we can turn on the heating from outside with a phone app. New apartment complexes also have shared facilities like a gym, a library, and delivery lockers. Life has definitely become more convenient. But in the past, neighbors all knew each other, and now I don't even know who lives next door. That's a little sad.
q-186092c412f8: What problems do people in your country have when they rent or buy a home? Tell me about the issues people talk about and how they deal with them.
a-aa2d8e1df462: In Korea, the problem people talk about most when it comes to housing is definitely the price. Especially in Seoul, homes are so expensive that buying one feels almost impossible for young people. So most of them rent, but deposits in Korea are very large, and many people have to take out a loan just to pay the deposit. The second problem is noise between floors. Since most people live in apartments, neighbors sometimes fight over footsteps or kids running upstairs, and it's often on the news. The third is when something breaks and the landlord is slow to fix it. When my boiler broke down, I didn't know who to call, and I panicked a little. q-a97733d22cad: How has traveling changed over the years? Compare the way people traveled in the past with the way they travel now.
a-e37d81c3f4c0: The way people travel has completely changed since I was young. In the past, if you wanted to travel, you usually went to a travel agency and booked a package tour. Traveling abroad was expensive, so it was only for special occasions. Now we do everything on our phones. We compare and book flights and hotels on apps, find our way with a map app, and read menus with a translation app. Thanks to low-cost airlines, traveling abroad has become much cheaper, too. So these days, independent trips and solo trips are more common than group tours. Another big change is that people visit cafes and restaurants they saw on social media rather than famous tourist sites. I prefer the way we travel now because there's much more freedom. But it's a little sad that we talk to local people less, since everyone is looking at their phones.
q-27dccad79de3: What concerns do people have when they travel these days? Tell me about the issues travelers talk about and what they do about them.
a-cffdb7164bab: I think the biggest concern for travelers these days is the cost. q-54e0bf545d55: Compare the activities that children do at parks with the activities that adults do at parks. What facilities are there for each group?
a-39af49bbfc0a: What children and adults do at parks is quite different. Children never sit still. For children, the park is a place to burn off energy. Adults are the opposite. Most of them come to rest or to exercise. So the facilities are different, too. For kids, there are playgrounds and water play areas, and for adults, there are bike paths, exercise machines, benches, and convenience stores. q-4abcf411d3b6: Tell me about some problems with public parks in your country these days. What causes them, and what should be done to solve them?
a-f4f0e997241b: I think the biggest problem with parks in Korea these days is trash. Electric scooters and bikes go too fast on the walking paths, so it's dangerous for people on foot, especially kids and older people. To solve these problems, we need more trash cans, but in the end, I think people's attitude matters most. There should be campaigns to take your own trash home, and people who break the speed limit should be fined. That way, parks will be more pleasant for everyone.
q-aec046a94be2: How has shopping changed over the years? Compare the way people shopped in the past with the way they shop now.
a-682b97526aa7: Shopping has changed completely since I was young. In the past, if you wanted to buy something, you had to go there in person. You could see and touch the products, and at the market, you could even bargain over the price. It took a long time, but there was a human touch. Now we buy almost everything on our phones. q-d1acb74702dd: What issues or concerns do people in your country have about shopping these days? Tell me what people are talking about and what you think about it.

q-2f91d6ae3f7f: Tell me about how recycling is done in your country. What kinds of things do people recycle, and how do you personally recycle at home? Describe each step.

But now it's just a habit, and I don't mind it at all. I think it's a small thing I can do for the environment.
q-68a0e7393538: Tell me about the weather and seasons in your country. How has the weather changed since you were a child?
a-279ed6a41dab: Korea has four distinct seasons. Spring is warm, and there are flowers everywhere, but there are also many days with bad fine dust. Summer is hot and humid, and there's a rainy season for a few weeks starting in late June. Fall is my favorite season because the sky is clear and the air is cool. It's the best time to run at Hangang Park. Winter is cold and dry, and it snows sometimes. But the weather has definitely changed since I was a child. Back then, spring and fall were long, and it snowed a lot in winter, so my younger brother and I used to make snowmen. These days, summer is much longer and hotter. I have to turn on the air conditioner from May, and last summer it was so hot at night that I couldn't sleep well. Spring and fall have become so short that they're over before you know it. q-8da3ec4271f2: Tell me about the banks in your country. What do they look like, where are they located, and what do people usually do there? Tell me about the last time you went to a bank.

q-676c55f6bf83: Tell me about the hotels in your country. What are they like? What do you usually do when you arrive at a hotel?

In tourist areas like Gangneung or Jeju, guesthouses and small family-run places are popular, too. When I travel, I usually stay at a mid-priced hotel with a nice view. When I arrive, I check in at the front desk first and ask what time breakfast is served. When I get to my room, the first thing I do is open the curtains and check the view. After resting for about ten minutes, I go right back out and walk around the neighborhood to see where the convenience stores and restaurants are. For me, a hotel isn't a place to spend a lot of time. It's a place to sleep and shower well. So the bed and the location matter more than the size.
q-ca19b1989263: What kinds of technology do people in your country use most often? How has technology changed compared to when you were young?
a-3164cfb18ae3: The technology Koreans use most is definitely the smartphone. On the subway, almost everyone is looking at their phone. I use mine all day, too. It's a huge change compared to when I was young. Back then, every device was separate. We made calls on a phone, listened to music on an MP3 player, and took pictures with a digital camera, and if we got lost, we asked someone for directions. We could only use the internet on a computer at home. Now all of that is in one device the size of my hand. Recently, people have started using AI a lot, too. I ask AI to correct my English sentences or to help me plan a trip. Life has become really convenient, but there are concerns as well. We spend too much time looking at screens, so I try not to use my phone for an hour before bed. I think in the future, how we control technology will matter more than how much we use it.
q-003aac0096a8: Tell me about the geography of your country. Are there mountains, rivers, or beaches? What do people do there? Also, tell me about a neighboring country and how it is different from yours.
a-90010fa04ad1: Korea is a peninsula, so it's surrounded by the sea on three sides. Also, about seventy percent of the country is mountains. They're not very high, but they're everywhere, so you can see mountains even from the middle of Seoul. That's why hiking is one of the most popular weekend activities. There are many big rivers, too, and the most famous one is the Han River, which runs through the middle of Seoul. I run along that river almost every week. On the east coast, there are beautiful beaches with clear water, like the ones in Gangneung, and in the south, there are lots of beautiful islands, like Jeju. In summer, people go to the beaches, and in fall, they go to the mountains to see the autumn leaves. As for a neighboring country, there's Japan. It's only two hours away by plane, and we have some things in common, like eating rice as our main food and using chopsticks. But Japan is an island country, so it has far more earthquakes, and cars drive on the left side of the road. When I visited Osaka, I was impressed by how quiet and clean the streets were. It's close, but the atmosphere is quite different.
q-5ec2ed4a2d32: What kinds of clothes do people in your country usually wear? How has fashion changed since you were young?
a-5a6c13e3fa20: These days, people in Korea dress quite casually. Comfortable clothes are the trend, so many people wear jeans or wide pants with sneakers, even on weekdays. Because we have four distinct seasons, what people wear changes a lot during the year. In summer, it's T-shirts and shorts, and in winter, almost everyone wears a long padded coat because it's so cold. Fashion has changed a lot since I was young. Back then, everyone followed the same trend. If a celebrity wore something on TV, you'd see the same jacket everywhere the next month. Now people care more about what suits them, and there are so many different styles on the street. The way we shop has changed, too. A lot of people buy clothes online and follow fashion accounts on social media. Personally, I keep it simple. I mostly wear dark colors and comfortable sneakers, and I still prefer to try clothes on at a department store before I buy them. For me, feeling comfortable matters more than looking trendy.
q-062a07aefcc5: What do people in your country do to stay healthy? How is that different from the past? What do you do for your health?
a-48e372935662: I think people in Korea care about their health more than ever. These days, a lot of young people go to the gym or join running clubs, and it's common to take vitamins every day. Many people also get a health checkup every year or two. It was quite different in the past. My parents' generation didn't really work out. They stayed healthy by eating home-cooked meals, walking a lot, and staying active all day. My mom still says that good food and good sleep are the best medicine. In my case, I started jogging two years ago after my health checkup. The doctor told me I needed to exercise more, and the gym felt too expensive, so I chose running because it's free. Now I run three times a week along the Han River. I also try to eat less delivery food and go to bed before midnight. I'm not perfect, but since I started, I get sick less often, and I have more energy. I think a healthy person is simply someone who exercises regularly, eats well, and sleeps enough.
q-0451a0d5fc1a: Tell me about the holidays in your country. What do people do on those days? Tell me about a memorable holiday you had.
a-f4a4e25f77d5: The two biggest holidays in Korea are Lunar New Year and Chuseok, which is like Korean Thanksgiving. On both holidays, families get together, prepare a lot of traditional food, and pay respect to their ancestors. On New Year's Day, we eat rice cake soup, and on Chuseok, we eat half-moon-shaped rice cakes. Children bow to their grandparents and get some pocket money, which was my favorite part when I was a kid. The problem is the traffic. Everyone travels to their hometown at the same time, so the highways are terribly crowded. These days, things are changing. More and more families keep the ceremonies simple, and some even travel abroad during the holidays. The holiday I remember best is last Chuseok. My parents live just outside Seoul, so I went there for two days. My mom and I made the rice cakes together, my younger brother came home, too, and we all played a traditional board game until midnight. I came back with a huge bag of side dishes. For me, holidays are really about eating together with my family.
q-d63da79f4bb8: Tell me about the appointments or plans you usually make with people. Where do you meet, and what do you do? Tell me about a time you had to cancel plans.
a-82b59e2d3c71: I usually make plans with my friends on weekends, because everyone is busy during the week. We decide the date and the place in a group chat, and it often takes a while because everyone's schedule is different. We usually meet near a subway station, in areas like Hongdae or Gangnam, since they're easy for everyone to get to. First we have dinner, and then we go to a cafe or have a beer and talk for hours. I try to arrive about ten minutes early, because I hate making people wait. Of course, plans don't always work out. Last summer, I was supposed to go to Busan with a friend for a week. But two days before we left, my friend got a bad flu, so we had to cancel everything. Luckily, the train tickets were fully refunded, and we only lost a small fee for the guesthouse. I was disappointed, but I ended up having a relaxing week at home. Since then, I always check the cancellation policy before I book anything.
q-914df84735fe: Tell me about the furniture or appliances in your home. Which one is your favorite? How are they different from the ones you had when you were a child?
a-1337c0d1c571: My apartment is small, so I don't have a lot of furniture. In the living room, there's a gray sofa, a small TV, and a bookshelf, and in the bedroom, I have a bed and a desk. My favorite piece of furniture is definitely the sofa. I moved it next to the window last summer, and now it's the best spot in my apartment. I read, watch movies, and even take naps there. It's very different from the furniture I grew up with. When I was a child, our furniture was big, heavy, and made of dark wood. My parents bought it when they got married and used it for decades. Now most of my furniture is small and light, and I put some of it together by myself. It's cheaper and easier to move, but it doesn't last as long. As for appliances, the ones I can't live without are the washing machine and the vacuum cleaner, because they save me so much time. And after my boiler broke down last winter, I learned how important it is to check them regularly.
q-bea9b163e4a6: What kinds of public transportation do people use in your country? What do you usually use, and why? How has it changed?
a-74267e3e8b31: Seoul has a great public transportation system. There are subways and buses that go almost everywhere, and they come every few minutes. You can use one transportation card or just your phone for everything, and you get a discount when you transfer between the bus and the subway. It's also quite cheap compared to other big cities. I usually take the subway, because there are no traffic jams, and it's always on time. I also like that I can listen to music or read on the way. The only downside is rush hour. The trains are so crowded that sometimes I can't even move my arms. Public transportation has changed a lot since I was young. In the past, we had to buy paper tickets and check a route map on the wall. Now an app tells me exactly when the next train arrives and which car is the least crowded. For longer trips, I take the KTX, the high-speed train. It gets me to Gangneung in just two hours, so I don't really need a car.
q-51759d665dec: Tell me about a restaurant you often go to or the food you order. How has eating out or food delivery changed in your country?
a-1497d39802ea: There's a small Korean restaurant near my place that I go to at least once a week. It's run by an older couple, and their kimchi stew is amazing. It's not fancy, but the food tastes like a home-cooked meal, and the side dishes are free and unlimited, which is normal in Korea. Since I live alone, I also order delivery two or three times a week. I usually order fried chicken, pizza, or Korean food through an app. Food delivery has changed a lot in Korea. In the past, we could only order Chinese food or fried chicken by phone, and we had to pay in cash. Now you can get almost anything within thirty minutes through an app, even a coffee or a single dessert. At Hangang Park, there are even special pickup zones for delivery food. It's really convenient, but there are downsides. Delivery fees keep going up, and all the disposable containers create a lot of trash. So these days, I try to cook more often and order delivery only on weekends.
q-0d244579a663: Tell me about the housework you do. How was housework shared in your family when you were a child?
a-20fe0036192a: Since I live alone, all the housework is on me. On weekdays, I keep it simple.
